summary: Five-row paged list window: a text-list scroller with five row records, left/right value cells and two page-number labels; built as a child part of another window (caller Ui_WindowPart_Ctor).
evidence: Ctor 0x00465978 calls Ui_Object_CtorSmallB (0x002CFACC), stores 0x00772008 in the object head and creates the scroller at +0x54 (vtable 0x0077F71C) via 0x00622248; InitPanes 0x004656F8 (vtable slot 8) binds txt_l1..txt_r1 and the pager (0x0062202C) and builds five 0xC-byte row records at +0x70.

fields.name: vtable
fields.evidence: Ctor stores 0x00772008 at offset 0; that vtable's slot 8 is Ui_FiveRowPagedWindow_InitPanes (0x004656F8). The first store 0x00760350 is the temporary Ui_Object_CtorSmallB vtable.

fields.name: rowCount
fields.evidence: The scroller created at +0x54 does [scroller+0x18] = 5 (= self+0x6C) and five 0xC-byte row records are then constructed at +0x70; the batch attributes the store to +0x18 because the ctor keeps the scroller pointer, not self.

fields.name: scroller
fields.evidence: Scroller/pager sub-object at +0x54: ctor 0x00622248(self+0x54, self) gives it vtable 0x0077F71C and five rows; 0x0062202C(&self->f_54, 10, 11) binds its pager_num_l/r labels in InitPanes.

fields.name: unknown_vtableCall34
fields.evidence: Not a data field: the evidence is a virtual call through the vtable at offset 0 (slot +0x34, the pane/text bind method), so 0xD0 is a field-extraction artefact and must not become a struct member.

fields.name: unknown_vtableCall38
fields.evidence: Not a data field: evidence is a virtual call through vtable slot +0x38 (null-text overlay bind), so 0xE0 is a field-extraction artefact.

evidence: Ctor 0x004CF548 (vtable 0x00778AF4) runs Ui_Object_CtorBase, clears +0x49 and +0x4C. maybe_Ui_MemberList_RemoveAtCursor (0x004CF870) reads the cursor index from self+0x38 and memmoves the 8 bytes at +0x49; the derived deleting dtor 0x004CFF74 (vtable 0x00778C84) destroys 8 x 0x50-byte rows at +0x54.

fields.name: vtable
fields.evidence: Ctor 0x004CF548 stores 0x00778AF4 at offset 0; the same vtable is installed by the base constructor and restored by the derived destructor (0x004CFF74 stores 0x00778C84).

fields.name: cursor
fields.evidence: 0x004CF870 reads self+0x38, returns 0 when null and otherwise uses the byte at cursor+0xC as the row index to remove; the field is a cursor object, not an integer.

fields.name: memberIdList
fields.evidence: self+0x49 is an 8-byte member-id list: the ctor clears byte 0 and maybe_Ui_MemberList_RemoveAtCursor shifts bytes from +0x4A down over it, so this is the first entry of an u8[8] array.

fields.name: maybe_selectedIndex
fields.evidence: Ctor clears the word at +0x4C; no reader appears in this batch, so only the zero initialisation supports a selected/active index.

fields.name: maybe_memberRows
fields.evidence: Eight 0x50-byte row objects start at +0x54: the derived deleting dtor 0x004CFF74 runs std_destroy_range(self+0x54, 0x003E04BC, 0x50, 8). The batch size 88 only covers the base head, not the full row array.

fields.name: vtable
fields.evidence: Offset 0 of each embedded sub-window receives a vtable (g_003D8A18..g_003D8A30); since the composite allocation begins with the first text window, its first word is that window's vtable.

fields.name: maybe_ringPrev
fields.evidence: piVar2[1] = piVar2 initialises a self-referential intrusive-ring link before the embedded windows are constructed; the damaged decompilation hides which sub-object owns it.

fields.name: maybe_ringNext
fields.evidence: piVar2[2] = piVar2 is the matching next link of the same empty ring initialised by the ctor.

fields.name: unknown_word_4c
fields.evidence: The stored value is 0x0075A2AC (vtable 0x0075A204 + 0xA8) written into the embedded Ui_CursorWindow, i.e. a sub-object's internal base/vtable word; it is not a data field of this composite.

summary: Seven-slot text label window owned by a list screen: fetches seven u16 entry ids from the list, compares them with the stored ids and updates the name text/visibility.
evidence: maybe_Ui_SevenSlotTextWindow_Update 0x003CF06C reads seven ids with func_00639C80, compares them with the pointer stored at +0x24C, and drives Ui_Element_SetFlagBit0(self->f_34, self->f_28<<16 | 3/4/5). The comparison is gated by f_25C % 60 == 0.

fields.name: paneGroupId
fields.evidence: Used as the high 16 bits of every element id: (u32)self->f_28 << 16 | 5 / | 3 / | 4 passed to Ui_Element_SetFlagBit0, i.e. the group id of the text element.

fields.name: element
fields.evidence: self->f_34 is the first argument of Ui_Element_SetFlagBit0(self->f_34, id, 0/1) for element ids 3, 4 and 5, so it is the UI element carrying the seven slot labels.

fields.name: prevSlotIds
fields.evidence: self->f_24C is dereferenced as a u16 array: seven (u16*)self->f_24C[i] values are compared against the seven ids fetched from the list, and the update returns early when it is null.

fields.name: slotIndex
fields.evidence: Byte counter: reset to 0 on a forced refresh, incremented (*(char*)(f_254) = uVar15+1) while walking slots and used as index into prevSlotIds ((byte*)(f_254) * 2).

fields.name: maybe_frameCounter
fields.evidence: Compared modulo 60 using the 0x88888889 multiply: f_25C + (f_25C * 0x88888889 >> 0x25) * -0x3C == 0, so the id comparison runs once per 60 frames.
